corridors.name: North–South
corridors.text: The busiest road in the region, carrying copper south and fuel and goods north.

corridors.name: Beira
corridors.text: Zimbabwe's shortest way to the sea.

corridors.name: Maputo
corridors.text: Links Gauteng to the nearest deep water port, about 90 km from the border.

corridors.name: Nacala
corridors.text: A natural deep harbour serving landlocked Malawi and eastern Zambia.

corridors.name: Dar es Salaam
corridors.text: The TAZARA railway, built in the 1970s to give Zambia an outlet that avoided Rhodesia and South Africa.

corridors.name: Lobito
corridors.text: The Benguela Railway, rebuilt after the Angolan war to carry copper west to the Atlantic.

corridors.name: Trans-Kalahari
corridors.text: A road across the Kalahari linking the Atlantic to Gauteng.

corridors.name: Walvis Bay–Ndola
corridors.text: Through the Caprivi Strip to the Copperbelt.
